// name: Scoped to @applyy (two y's) per the naming standard; the folder still reads applyyy pending Teja's rename.
name: @applyy/shared-types
// version: 0.0.0 because nothing is published to a registry — this is a workspace-internal package only.
// private: Belt-and-braces against an accidental `pnpm publish` of a repo that contains resume and CTC data.
// type: ESM everywhere: Deno Edge Functions cannot consume CommonJS, and the Node worker is ESM too.
// exports: Source-only export map. There is no build step: Deno type-checks .ts directly and Vite/tsx transpile it, so shipping compiled output would add a build to every peer's inner loop for zero benefit.
// types: Redundant with exports for modern resolvers, kept for editors that still read this field.
// files: Only src ships if this ever is packed; no stray configs.
// scripts.typecheck: Type-checks src AND test. The package has no runtime code to build.
// scripts.test: Enum/table/graph parity against supabase/migrations. node --test runs .ts directly via native type stripping, so this needs no runner dependency and no build. It reads the migration FILES, never a database, so it works with no Supabase running.
// devDependencies: @types/node is needed by the PARITY TEST ONLY (node:fs, node:test, node:path, node:url); src/ deliberately uses no Node API, because the contract is imported by Deno Edge Functions and by the browser, so a Node builtin leaking into it would break two of three runtimes at runtime rather than at compile time. NOTE: this explanation lives at the top level because pnpm VALIDATES dependency names — a "// x" pseudo-key inside devDependencies is rejected with ERR_PNPM_INVALID_DEPENDENCY_NAME, the same trap as TS5025 inside compilerOptions. The trick is only safe in objects nothing validates. typescript is a devDependency here so the package can be type-checked standalone in CI; the root pins the actual version. The floor is 5.8, NOT 5.6: tsconfig.base.json sets erasableSyntaxOnly, which TypeScript only understands from 5.8 — under 5.6 it is an unknown-option error, so a lockfile refresh that resolved the caret down would break this package with no code change to blame. Raised 2026-09-10 to state the real requirement instead of relying on the caret floating to 5.9.
